options.A: Subcutaneous emphysema in the neck
options.B: Ventilator-associated pneumonia
options.C: Pneumothorax from alveolar rupture
options.D: Tension pneumothorax development

explanation: Spot on! Pneumonia is an infection caused by germs, whereas things like a collapsed lung (pneumothorax) happen from high pressure popping the delicate air sacs.

question: Why might a nurse relax a patient's long-standing diabetic diet restrictions during palliative care?

options.A: Sugar has no effect on blood glucose in terminal patients
options.B: Strict dietary control is no longer relevant to their comfort and quality of life
options.C: Diabetes automatically cures itself in advanced illness
options.D: Patients with terminal illnesses can no longer taste sweetness

explanation: You nailed it! Chronic disease rules are meant for long-term health. In palliative care, bringing a smile with a sweet treat matters much more.

question: What does a 4+ reflex score with jerky muscle spasms (clonus) usually point to?

options.A: Normal healthy muscle recovery
options.B: Complete peripheral nerve damage
options.C: Central nervous system pathology
options.D: Severe dehydration and low sodium

explanation: Extremely brisk reflexes with clonus mean there is likely an issue or irritation in the central nervous system (brain or spinal cord).

question: When do primary menstrual cramps usually hurt the most?

options.A: Exactly halfway through the normal menstrual cycle
options.B: During the first twenty-four hours of menstruation
options.C: On the final day when bleeding has nearly stopped
options.D: Two weeks before the menstrual bleeding begins

explanation: Spot on! Prostaglandin levels peak right at the start of your period, which is why the first day is usually the most painful.

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care in advanced degenerative disorders?

options.A: Stopping all forms of nursing care
options.B: Curing the genetic disease completely
options.C: Comfort and symptom management
options.D: Increasing rigorous physical therapy

explanation: Palliative care centers on relieving pain and distressing symptoms to ensure the patient remains comfortable and maintains their dignity. Beautiful nursing philosophy!

question: What is the main role of the nurse when working as part of an interprofessional healthcare team?

options.A: Performing all physical and occupational therapy sessions alone
options.B: Handling only the financial and discharge paperwork for the hospital
options.C: Overriding decisions made by physicians and therapists
options.D: Acting as the central coordinator who synthesizes updates from all disciplines

explanation: Because you are at the bedside around the clock, you bring together updates from doctors, therapists, and dietitians to keep everyone on the same page!

question: What local complication can happen if topical corticosteroids are used in thick layers for too long?

options.A: Complete numbness of the area
options.B: Skin thinning and atrophy
options.C: Excessive permanent tanning
options.D: Rapid growth of thick hair

explanation: Prolonged and improper application of potent topical steroids breaks down collagen in the skin, resulting in thinning, fragility, and striae. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h3)

question: Your patient just had shoulder surgery and is on bed rest. What is your next best move regarding AROM?

options.A: Encourage the patient to swing the arm rapidly to build strength quickly.
options.B: Check the medical orders and surgeon guidelines before allowing shoulder movement.
options.C: Ignore the surgery and start full arm rotations immediately.
options.D: Refuse to let the patient move any part of their entire body.

explanation: Always check the surgeon's rules first after an operation to make sure you protect the healing surgical site.

question: A mother calls worried about a yellowish crust forming over her baby's healing circumcision. What is this?

options.A: Normal granulation tissue part of the healing process
options.B: Leftover residue from petroleum jelly ointment
options.C: A sign of a severe bacterial wound infection
options.D: Dried urine crystals from frequent wet diapers

explanation: No need to panic! That yellowish film is a normal part of how skin heals down there—reassure the mother it's not pus or an infection.

question: What keeps a Foley urinary catheter securely in place inside the bladder?

options.A: Special surgical glue applied to the inner thigh skin
options.B: A tight plastic clamp attached around the external tubing
options.C: An inflated water balloon near the catheter tip
options.D: Natural suction created by the urine collection bag

explanation: Brilliant! Once the catheter is inside the bladder, we fill a tiny balloon with sterile water so it acts like an anchor and won't slip out.

question: How is chronic urinary retention different from acute urinary retention?

options.A: It involves painful spasms of the ureters.
options.B: It causes complete kidney shutdown right away.
options.C: It develops slowly and is often painless.
options.D: It only happens to younger female patients.

explanation: Because chronic retention builds up gradually, the bladder stretches out slowly over time, so the patient usually doesn't feel severe, sudden pain. Great job thinking it through!

question: Aside from giving fluids, what type of medication is routinely given right away if an infected (septic) abortion is suspected?

options.A: Long-acting oral hypoglycemic agents
options.B: Broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics
options.C: Topical corticosteroid ointments
options.D: Inhaled short-acting beta-agonists

explanation: Infection spreads fast! Starting broad-spectrum IV antibiotics early stops bacteria in their tracks and prevents the patient from sliding into full septic shock.

question: Why should a 38-year-old client who gets migraines with aura avoid combined oral contraceptives?

options.A: It triggers severe allergic skin rashes on the face
options.B: It will cause her migraines to happen every single day
options.C: It significantly increases her risk of having a stroke
options.D: It stops the migraine medication from working properly

explanation: This is a classic safety rule in pharmacology: migraines with aura, plus estrogen, plus being over 35 multiplies the risk of a dangerous stroke.

question: Why is angiogenesis so important for a growing malignant tumor?

options.A: It supplies necessary oxygen and nutrients while removing waste
options.B: It prevents the immune system from noticing the tumor mass
options.C: It encapsulates the tumor to keep it from spreading locally
options.D: It repairs damaged DNA inside the fast-growing cancer cells

explanation: You got it! Without a fresh blood supply delivering nutrients and carrying away waste, a tumor would quickly starve and stop growing.

question: Which of these is a valid medical reason to put in an indwelling urinary catheter?

options.A: General urinary incontinence with no skin breakdown
options.B: To make things easier for nursing staff during busy night shifts
options.C: Accurate hourly urine output measurement in a critically ill patient
options.D: The patient prefers not to get up to use the toilet at night

explanation: Spot on! We only use indwelling catheters when there is a strong medical need, like closely tracking kidney function in very sick patients.

question: Which of these is NOT a good reason to be careful with the Kubler-Ross model?

options.A: It guarantees every patient will have a completely painless death
options.B: Treating the stages as strict rules can hurt individualized care
options.C: It might miss cultural differences in how people grieve
options.D: Patients often skip or repeat stages

explanation: Spot on! The model maps out emotions—it has nothing to do with curing physical pain or guaranteeing a pain-free passing.

question: Why do nurses take a detailed health history when assessing a patient's blood (haematological) health?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial cost of patient care
options.B: To catch subtle clues about blood and clotting abnormalities
options.C: To diagnose the exact type of cancer immediately
options.D: To replace the need for routine laboratory blood tests

explanation: Spotting early clues in a patient's history helps you catch blood and clotting issues before they become serious. Great job thinking like a nurse!

question: Why must the packaging used for steam sterilization be porous (able to let air and steam through)?

options.A: To ensure the wrapper dissolves completely inside the machine
options.B: To make the heavy trays lighter for nurses to carry
options.C: To let air escape so the package smells fresh when opened
options.D: To allow the sterilizing agent to penetrate and reach the instruments

explanation: Brilliant! Steam needs to touch every single surface of the tools inside to actually kill the germs. Porous wraps let the steam in safely.

question: What exactly is caregiver burnout?

options.A: A formal diagnosis of depression given by a psychiatrist
options.B: The financial bankruptcy caused by buying medical equipment
options.C: Physical and emotional exhaustion from continuous caregiving duties
options.D: The intentional neglect of an older adult by family

explanation: Looking after someone day in and day out without enough rest can drain a person completely. That heavy fatigue is what we call burnout.

question: Which type of ultrasound is best when you need to check how fast and in what direction blood is flowing?

options.A: Doppler ultrasound
options.B: Static X-ray mode
options.C: M-Mode ultrasound
options.D: B-Mode ultrasound

explanation: Doppler is your go-to scan for blood vessels because it specifically tracks moving red blood cells to measure flow.

question: Why must work inside the TSSU always flow in one direction?

options.A: To reduce the electricity consumption of heavy sterilizing machines
options.B: To prevent clean and sterile items from mixing with dirty ones
options.C: To make it easier for nursing students to clean the floors
options.D: To speed up the physical movement of heavy instrument trays

explanation: Exactly! Keeping a one-way workflow ensures items only move forward from dirty to clean, protecting patients from cross-contamination.

question: Why do we apply a tourniquet to a patient's arm before trying to insert an IV cannula?

options.A: To sterilize the outer skin surface before cleaning
options.B: To completely stop arterial blood flow to the limb
options.C: To numb the local skin area and reduce sharp pain
options.D: To trap venous blood and make the veins swell up

explanation: Exactly! The tourniquet pauses blood from returning to the heart, causing the veins underneath to plump up so they are much easier to see and feel.

question: At which spinal level is an intrathecal injection usually performed in adults to avoid damaging the spinal cord?

options.A: C1-C2 or C2-C3
options.B: L3-L4 or L4-L5
options.C: T1-T2 or T2-T3
options.D: S1-S2 or S2-S3

explanation: In adults, the spinal cord ends around the L1-L2 vertebra, so punctures are done lower down at lumbar levels to keep the cord safe. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h2)

question: Your patient is scheduled for an MRI, but mentions they have a permanent heart pacemaker. What should you do right away?

options.A: Wrap the patient's chest in a lead apron to block the magnetic field
options.B: Administer a mild sedative to calm the patient before the scan starts
options.C: Proceed with the scan because pacemakers are safe inside the magnet
options.D: Notify the ordering physician and the radiology department immediately

explanation: Hold on! That giant magnet can pull on metal implants and ruin a pacemaker. Always flag this to the team immediately to keep the patient safe.

question: Which specific questionnaire is widely used to screen mothers for postpartum depression?

options.A: Apgar scoring system
options.B: Bishop cervical score
options.C: Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale
options.D: Glasgow Coma Scale

explanation: Spot on! The Edinburgh scale is a short, trusted questionnaire designed to help nurses catch signs of depression in new mothers early.

question: What does the abbreviation LMP stand for in nursing assessments?

options.A: Last menstrual period
options.B: Luteal menstrual phase
options.C: Low mucosal pressure
options.D: Latest medical procedure

explanation: Easy and essential! LMP means Last Menstrual Period—a super important detail you will ask almost every female patient.

question: Which of these is a great example of an open-ended question you can ask a patient?

options.A: Asking 'How are you coping with your illness today?'
options.B: Nodding silently without asking any questions at all
options.C: Asking 'Did you take your morning blood pressure pill?'
options.D: Telling the patient 'You need to stop worrying so much.'

explanation: Well done! Open-ended questions can't be answered with a simple 'yes' or 'no', which encourages your patient to open up and share more.

question: What is the name of the smooth, triangular area found on the inner floor of the bladder?

options.A: The renal pelvis
options.B: The meatus
options.C: The glomerulus
options.D: The trigone

explanation: It's called the trigone (think 'triangle'). It is marked out by the openings of your two ureters and your urethra, and germs love to hang out here during bladder infections.

question: Why do nurses do an evaluation at the end of a care plan?

options.A: To determine if the patient met their health goals
options.B: To calculate the total cost of hospital supplies used
options.C: To assign blame if a complication occurs during recovery
options.D: To write a formal discharge report for insurance companies

explanation: Evaluation simply checks whether your nursing actions actually helped the patient reach their health targets. You're tracking success!

question: Which post-sigmoidoscopy symptom means a patient might have a bowel perforation and needs emergency care?

options.A: Suddenly feeling very sleepy and tired
options.B: Passing frequent gas in the first couple of hours
options.C: Sudden, severe worsening belly pain with a hard, rigid stomach
options.D: Finding a tiny streak of bright red blood on the toilet paper once

explanation: Good catch! A rigid, intensely painful belly is a major red flag for a bowel tear (perforation) and needs immediate medical attention.

question: What is a key nursing action when caring for a patient taking a diuretic medication?

options.A: Check pupil reactions every fifteen minutes
options.B: Accurately monitor intake and output
options.C: Encourage a high-sodium snack diet
options.D: Restrict the patient from walking entirely

explanation: Spot on! Tracking what goes in and what comes out tells us if the diuretic is doing its job safely without causing dehydration.

question: In Nigeria, which setting usually records the lowest fertility rates?

options.A: Rural farming villages
options.B: Remote agrarian settlements
options.C: Urban centers
options.D: Nomadic pastoral communities

explanation: Correct! City dwellers often have smaller family sizes due to higher living costs and better access to school and family planning.

question: Why does a doctor order liver function blood tests for a patient with upper tummy pain?

options.A: To measure the exact amount of food remaining in the stomach
options.B: To see if the patient has a normal blood pressure
options.C: To check for inflammation or damage in the liver and biliary system
options.D: To determine how quickly the kidneys are filtering waste

explanation: When liver cells or bile ducts get irritated or damaged, they leak specific enzymes into the blood. The lab tests catch this! Great job thinking clinically.

question: What is the main goal of chemoprophylaxis?

options.A: To prevent an infection before it develops or turns active
options.B: To cure a chronic autoimmune disease permanently
options.C: To destroy normal healthy flora in the gut
options.D: To replace surgical hand hygiene in hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Chemoprophylaxis is just a medical term for using medications to stop an infection before it even starts.

question: How does FGM commonly affect a woman's sexual health later in life?

options.A: It has zero impact on sexual function or emotional wellbeing
options.B: It can cause painful intercourse and reduced sexual sensitivity
options.C: It increases sensitivity and enhances sexual pleasure
options.D: It only affects fertility without altering sexual sensations

explanation: You're doing great! Because sensitive nerve endings and tissues are damaged or removed, many women face pain and decreased sensation.

question: You finish helping a patient and notice visible blood on your bare hands. What is your immediate next step?

options.A: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and running water
options.B: Apply an alcohol-based hand rub and rub briskly
options.C: Put on clean gloves without washing the hands
options.D: Wipe the hands clean with a dry paper towel

explanation: Right! When hands are visibly soiled with blood or body fluids, soap and water are a must because alcohol rubs can't wash away the physical dirt.

question: Why is teaching the family of a neurological patient just as important as teaching the patient?

options.A: Doctors refuse to talk to anyone except the patient's spouse
options.B: Family members are legally required to pass nursing board exams
options.C: Patients with brain disorders completely lose the ability to speak
options.D: Family members often provide long-term care at home after discharge

explanation: Once the patient goes home, the family usually takes over daily care. Training them well means the patient stays safe and healthy after leaving the hospital.

question: Why do those misplaced patches of tissue cause so much pain during a woman's period?

options.A: It causes the ovaries to stop producing estrogen entirely
options.B: The trapped blood immediately turns into malignant tumors
options.C: The blood attracts white blood cells that release healing enzymes
options.D: The body has no natural exit route for the blood, leading to irritation

explanation: Think of it this way: that misplaced tissue still bleeds when period time comes, but it has nowhere to flow out. This trapped blood causes irritation and painful swelling.

question: Which drink should you avoid giving a child right after a tonsillectomy?

options.A: Vanilla ice cream
options.B: Clear apple juice
options.C: Red-colored juice
options.D: Plain cold water

explanation: You got it! Stay away from red drinks because if the patient throws up, the red color looks just like fresh blood and causes unnecessary panic.

question: How is 'wellness' best understood in nursing?

options.A: The total elimination of chronic disease through surgical intervention
options.B: The complete absence of any physical or psychological discomfort
options.C: An active, lifelong process of making choices toward optimal well-being
options.D: A temporary state that only occurs when a person is admitted to a ward

explanation: Great job! Wellness isn't just about not being sick; it's a daily, lifelong journey of making healthy choices for your mind and body.

question: What is the best way to interpret a child's weight measurement in a clinic?

options.A: Averaging the weight reading with the mother's weight
options.B: Plotting the measurement on a growth chart to observe the growth trend over time
options.C: Checking if the weight matches the child's shoe size and hair color
options.D: Comparing the child's weight directly to the average weight of an adult

explanation: A single number doesn't tell the whole story. Seeing how the weight tracks on a growth curve over months shows the true picture of health!

question: Which of these nursing actions is NOT a priority when caring for a patient having an acute sickle cell pain crisis?

options.A: Providing adequate hydration with intravenous fluids
options.B: Administering prescribed analgesics for pain relief
options.C: Administering supplemental oxygen if oxygen saturation is low
options.D: Administering scheduled doses of oral iron supplements

explanation: Iron pills won't help during a sickle cell crisis and could be harmful. The main goals during a crisis are keeping the patient well-hydrated, giving oxygen if needed, and managing their pain!

question: Why is it unhelpful to just write off a family planning defaulter as simply 'uncooperative'?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will never return to the facility
options.B: It breaks hospital regulations regarding patient confidentiality
options.C: It automatically makes the client pregnant within a week
options.D: It ignores practical barriers and personal reasons driving the missed appointment

explanation: People miss appointments for real reasons—like side effects, transport costs, or busy schedules. Looking past the label helps us solve the actual problem together.

question: What is the primary function of the transverse pontine fibers?

options.A: Carrying visual signals to the occipital lobe
options.B: Linking spinal nerves to the olfactory bulb
options.C: Connecting the cerebral cortex to the cerebellum
options.D: Transmitting pain signals directly to the thalamus

explanation: These fibers act like a major highway linking your thinking brain (cerebrum) with your coordination center (cerebellum).

question: What is the name of the muscular food pipe that connects your throat to your stomach?

options.A: Larynx
options.B: Pharynx
options.C: Trachea
options.D: Esophagus

explanation: Spot on! The esophagus is our dedicated highway for swallowing food down from the throat to the stomach.

question: What happens to a health facility if DRF medicines are priced way too low?

options.A: The facility will experience severe drug stock-outs
options.B: Private pharmacies will close down due to competition
options.C: The government will increase funding immediately
options.D: The pharmacy will accumulate excessive cash reserves

explanation: Makes sense, right? If you sell medicines below what it costs to buy them, the money runs out, and soon there are simply no drugs left on the pharmacy shelves for patients.

question: When examining the tummy, why do we listen (auscultate) before we press (palpate)?

options.A: Auscultation requires deep pressure that must be done first.
options.B: Patients find palpation relaxing after listening to bowel sounds.
options.C: Palpation can alter or stimulate bowel sounds, making them inaccurate.
options.D: Standard hospital policy dictates this order for all body systems.

explanation: You're doing great! If you press or massage the tummy first, you wake up the bowels and make them make extra noise. Always listen first to catch their natural sounds!

question: Which units are standard for recording height and weight in clinical nursing notes?

options.A: Feet and pounds
options.B: Centimeters and kilograms
options.C: Millimeters and grams
options.D: Inches and stones

explanation: Hospitals use the metric system (centimeters and kilograms) worldwide to keep records clear and prevent medication dosing mistakes.

question: What is the main purpose of using standard anatomical terminology in nursing practice?

options.A: To ensure clear and accurate communication among healthcare workers
options.B: To replace the need for physical assessments in the ward
options.C: To make patient medical records harder for families to read
options.D: To provide complex billing codes for hospital management

explanation: Standardized terms prevent misunderstandings so that every nurse or doctor knows the exact location being discussed. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the main thing we look at in haematological tests?

options.A: Electrical activity in the heart
options.B: Lung capacity and breathing
options.C: Kidney filtration and urine output
options.D: Blood and blood-making tissues

explanation: Haematology is all about studying blood cells and the tissues, like bone marrow, that make them. You've got this!

question: Why is recording how well the patient tolerated the exercise so important for the care team?

options.A: It serves as a legal punishment if the patient is lazy.
options.B: It determines the exact hospital discharge date immediately.
options.C: It stops nurses from having to write shift reports.
options.D: It helps guide future exercise plans and shows recovery progress.

explanation: Tracking progress helps the whole healthcare team decide whether to keep the routine the same or step it up next time!

question: What should you do right away if your patient feels sharp belly cramps while you are running the fluid?

options.A: Stop the flow immediately until the cramp passes
options.B: Ignore the symptom as a normal expected reaction
options.C: Raise the fluid container higher to finish quickly
options.D: Push the rectal tube deeper into the sigmoid colon

explanation: Cramping means the bowel is filling up too fast! Always pause the flow and let the patient relax before starting again.

question: What is the main danger associated with postpartum hemorrhage in new mothers?

options.A: Permanent loss of the ability to walk
options.B: Severe allergic reactions to routine food
options.C: Chronic high blood pressure lasting years
options.D: Sudden and severe blood loss leading to shock

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage involves heavy bleeding after birth, which can quickly drop blood pressure and cause life-threatening shock if untreated. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h2)

question: What is the very first thing you must do when the AED tells everyone to 'stand clear'?

options.A: Check the patient's pulse at the carotid artery.
options.B: Press the shock button immediately without waiting.
options.C: Administer a rescue breath using a bag-valve-mask.
options.D: Ensure nobody is touching the patient.

explanation: Safety first! If anyone is touching the patient, the AED might misread the heart rhythm—or worse, give someone else a shock.

question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of normal wound healing that a patient should expect?

options.A: A thin line of pinkness near the cut
options.B: Pus draining from the incision site
options.C: Dry scabbing along the suture line
options.D: Mild tenderness around the edges

explanation: Pus indicates a bacterial infection and is never a normal part of wound healing. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h6)

question: At what specific time intervals is the Apgar score routinely performed on a newborn?

options.A: One and five minutes after birth
options.B: Immediately at birth and thirty minutes later
options.C: Ten and twenty minutes after birth
options.D: Every fifteen minutes for the first hour

explanation: The Apgar score is systematically calculated at one minute and five minutes after birth to evaluate the newborn's immediate adjustment to extrauterine life and response to resuscitation if needed. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h1)

question: Which alternative exit route for drugs is especially important for nurses to remember when caring for breastfeeding mothers?

options.A: Mammary excretion
options.B: Sweat gland secretion
options.C: Salivary elimination
options.D: Pulmonary excretion

explanation: Drugs can pass into breast milk through the mammary glands. As nurses, we always check if a mother's medications are safe for her breastfeeding infant!

question: You need to help turn a heavy patient in bed. Which movement should you avoid to protect your back?

options.A: Adjusting the bed to a comfortable working height
options.B: Twisting your waist while pulling the patient toward you
options.C: Widening your stance to create a stable base of support
options.D: Asking a colleague to help you slide the patient

explanation: Never twist your back while lifting or pulling! Always pivot with your feet instead to save your spinal discs from injury.

question: How can you deliver holistic care even when working in a busy, understaffed ward?

options.A: By refusing to admit any new patients until the workload lightens
options.B: By delegating all patient contact completely to hospital security guards
options.C: By ignoring all physical medication duties to focus entirely on meditation
options.D: By weaving compassionate communication and a reassuring touch into routine tasks

explanation: Brilliant! Holism doesn't always require extra time. You can easily integrate it into regular nursing duties like bathing a patient or administering medications.

question: A patient is having a hard time buttoning their shirt and holding a toothbrush after a stroke. Who should step in to help with these daily tasks?

options.A: Physical therapist
options.B: Speech-language pathologist
options.C: Physiatrist
options.D: Occupational therapist

explanation: Occupational therapists are experts at helping patients regain fine motor skills for daily activities like dressing, eating, and brushing teeth.

question: Why do Registered Nurses rely so much on updates from nursing assistants?

options.A: Assistants spend the most direct time observing daily changes
options.B: RNs are not permitted to enter patient rooms independently
options.C: Assistants are legally required to sign off on drug charts
options.D: Hospital policies mandate daily verbal briefings from staff

explanation: Because nursing assistants spend the most time helping with everyday tasks, they are often the first ones to notice tiny shifts in how a patient is feeling.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical cause of a bulging fontanelle?

options.A: Increased intracranial pressure
options.B: Meningitis
options.C: Mild dehydration
options.D: Hydrocephalus

explanation: You got it! Dehydration causes a sunken fontanelle, not a bulging one.

question: Why can a patient with a chronic illness still be placed toward the high-wellness end of the continuum?

options.A: Chronic illnesses automatically cure themselves over time
options.B: Medical tests cannot detect chronic conditions on the continuum
options.C: A chronic diagnosis means the disease has completely gone away
options.D: They can achieve a good quality of life and manage their symptoms well

explanation: Wellness involves mental and social well-being alongside physical status, allowing people with chronic conditions to feel well. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which immediate complication happens when an instrument accidentally punctures the muscular wall of the uterus during a procedure?

options.A: Secondary amenorrhea
options.B: Cervical incompetence
options.C: Gestational trophoblastic disease
options.D: Uterine perforation

explanation: Uterine perforation occurs when sharp instruments or foreign objects poke a hole right through the wall of the uterus. It's a surgical emergency you'll want to watch out for during recovery!

question: A client with severe hypertension asks for oral contraceptive pills. What should the nurse do during the assessment?

options.A: Identify hypertension as a contraindication and discuss safer alternative methods
options.B: Prescribe the pills immediately because blood pressure does not matter
options.C: Refuse to check the client's blood pressure during the visit
options.D: Tell the client that birth control pills cure high blood pressure

explanation: Estrogen-containing pills can worsen high blood pressure and increase stroke risk, so nurses must screen for medical conditions and offer safer choices like progestin-only options. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h5)

question: What is the main drawback of relying only on a chemical indicator strip on the outside of a sterile pack?

options.A: It can tell the exact internal temperature reached deep inside the metal tray
options.B: It permanently destroys the bacterial spores hidden inside the pack
options.C: It requires a laboratory incubator to read the final color change
options.D: It only shows that the pack was exposed to heat or gas, not that it is truly sterile

explanation: Color changes on the outside just prove the pack went into the machine; they don't guarantee every single germ inside was destroyed.

question: What is the very first nursing priority when caring for a patient who is heavily intoxicated?

options.A: Asking the patient to sign a treatment contract
options.B: Maintaining airway, breathing, and circulation
options.C: Exploring childhood causes of substance use
options.D: Teaching about the long-term dangers of drugs

explanation: Correct! Always remember your ABCs first. Keeping the patient breathing and stable is always our top emergency priority before anything else.

question: Which nursing intervention is essential for managing patients with hormone imbalances affecting fluid and electrolytes?

options.A: Tracking fluid intake and output records accurately
options.B: Restricting all forms of physical movement in bed
options.C: Applying warm compresses to the thyroid gland daily
options.D: Checking visual acuity every two hours around the clock

explanation: Monitoring fluid balance helps nurses catch early signs of dangerous electrolyte shifts and kidney stress caused by hormonal changes. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h6)

question: When should discharge planning and home safety talk begin in rehab?

options.A: Only after the patient returns to their home
options.B: When family members complain about lack of preparation
options.C: Early in the rehabilitation admission process
options.D: On the exact morning of the patient's discharge

explanation: Spot on! Starting early gives families enough time to get home modifications and training ready before discharge day.

question: A patient tells you they have a terrible headache. What kind of data is this?

options.A: Subjective data
options.B: Diagnostic data
options.C: Secondary data
options.D: Objective data

explanation: You got this! Subjective data is what the patient tells you (their symptoms and feelings). Since you can't measure a headache with a machine, it's subjective. Think 'S' for Subjective and 'S' for Spoken by the patient!

question: Why must drugs chosen for the formulary stay stable in tropical climates?

options.A: To make the drug containers look attractive on hospital shelves
options.B: To ensure the tablets dissolve instantly when dropped in cold water
options.C: To prevent the medicine from degrading rapidly under local weather conditions
options.D: to guarantee the medication smells pleasant during administration

explanation: Nigeria's warm weather can break down chemicals quickly. Drugs must be tough enough to hold their strength in our local climate!

question: Why does the foetal body redirect blood to the brain and heart during low oxygen states?

options.A: To speed up the growth of skin and digestive tissues
options.B: To protect the most vital organs from permanent damage
options.C: To increase the overall temperature of the amniotic fluid
options.D: To prepare the lungs for breathing air after birth

explanation: The body prioritizes survival by ensuring oxygen-rich blood reaches critical centers like the brain and heart first. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h1)

question: What is the main muscle cell that makes up the heart wall?

options.A: Osteocyte
options.B: Nephron
options.C: Cardiocyte
options.D: Neuron

explanation: You've got this! A cardiocyte is simply the individual muscle cell found in cardiac tissue. Nephrons are in the kidneys, neurons in the brain, and osteocytes in bones.

question: What is the primary purpose of giving a patient a naloxone kit upon discharge for opioid use?

options.A: To cure the underlying brain changes caused by long-term addiction
options.B: To reverse a potential life-threatening opioid overdose
options.C: To prevent the daily cravings for heroin or prescription pills
options.D: To serve as a daily vitamin replacement during recovery

explanation: Naloxone is an opioid antagonist that rapidly blocks opioid receptors, restoring normal breathing during an accidental overdose. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h6)

question: What is the normal, healthy job of proto-oncogenes in our bodies?

options.A: Triggering cell suicide immediately
options.B: Encapsulating benign tumors
options.C: Promoting normal cell growth and division
options.D: Repairing broken DNA strands

explanation: Spot on! Proto-oncogenes are normal, helpful genes that tell cells when it's time to grow and repair tissues.

question: What immediate emergency action should you take if the chest tube accidentally pulls loose from the drainage machine?

options.A: Submerge the end of the tubing in sterile water to maintain a seal
options.B: Leave the tubing completely open to the room air without protection
options.C: Wash the disconnected plastic ends with soap and tap water
options.D: Clamp the patient's chest tube tightly and leave the room to find help

explanation: Brilliant! Putting the tube tip into sterile water creates an instant temporary water seal, keeping room air out of the patient's chest while you grab a new system.

question: Which group of symptoms strongly points to a pelvic infection (sepsis) after an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Painless vaginal bleeding and elevated blood pressure
options.B: High fever, foul-smelling discharge, and lower abdominal pain
options.C: Frequent urination, clear discharge, and normal temperature
options.D: Severe headache, blurred vision, and dry skin

explanation: Think of infection signs: fever, bad-smelling discharge, and tummy pain are classic red flags that unsterile instruments or tissue were left behind.

question: What is an emerging infectious disease?

options.A: A genetic illness passed down from parents to their children
options.B: A well-known infection that is now completely eradicated worldwide
options.C: A chronic condition caused by long-term environmental pollution
options.D: An entirely new infection or one rapidly spreading into new areas

explanation: Emerging infections are newly recognized in human populations or are spreading to new geographic regions where they were previously unknown. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h1)

question: What should you do if you spot an item on the sterile table and you are not totally sure if it is sterile?

options.A: Consider it contaminated and remove it from the field immediately
options.B: Ask the surgeon if it looks clean enough to use anyway
options.C: Wipe the item down with an alcohol swab and place it back
options.D: Leave it alone until the end of the surgical procedure

explanation: When in doubt, throw it out! The golden rule of theatre asepsis is that if sterility is questionable, the item is dirty.

question: An antibiotic costs 500 Naira to land in the pharmacy, and hospital policy adds a 20 percent mark-up. What is the retail price?

options.A: 520 Naira
options.B: 550 Naira
options.C: 600 Naira
options.D: 700 Naira

explanation: Let's do the quick math: 20 percent of 500 Naira is 100 Naira. Add that mark-up to the original 500 Naira cost, and you get a final retail price of 600 Naira. Easy peasy!

question: What is the primary purpose of performing a gastric lavage on a patient?

options.A: To measure daily digestive enzyme production in the pancreas
options.B: To provide long-term nutritional support for unconscious patients
options.C: To relieve chronic constipation by clearing the lower bowels
options.D: To remove ingested poisons from the stomach before they are absorbed

explanation: Gastric lavage acts as an emergency washing technique specifically targeted at flushing out harmful substances from the upper gastrointestinal tract before systemic absorption takes place. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h1)

question: A nurse is teaching a parent how to help their child complete homework without getting overwhelmed. What strategy is best to recommend?

options.A: Force the child to finish everything in one long session
options.B: Break large assignments into smaller, manageable steps
options.C: Ignore the homework struggles so the child learns independently
options.D: Punish the child whenever a mistake is made on paper

explanation: Breaking tasks down reduces cognitive overload and anxiety for children who struggle with processing large amounts of information. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the main limitation of a chemical indicator strip placed inside an instrument tray?

options.A: It can only be read using an ultraviolet microscope
options.B: It dissolves completely if the steam pressure gets too high
options.C: It only measures the external room temperature of the storage area
options.D: It shows that conditions for sterilization occurred, but not that spores are dead

explanation: Chemical strips change color when exposed to heat or steam, which proves the machine got hot enough. However, they don't test actual germ survival like biological tests do.

question: You need to move a heavy patient from a stretcher to a bed. What is the safest move?

options.A: Ask the patient to jump across while you hold their hands
options.B: Use a mechanical lift and ask another colleague to help
options.C: Pull the patient quickly using your arm muscles alone
options.D: Bend your back completely straight to gain extra lifting power

explanation: Teamwork and mechanical aids save your back! Never try to lift a heavy patient all by yourself.
